summary: Full E2E validation of Iter-76 Profile Level & Progression System — 6/6 backend gap pytests pass + all 8 frontend review-request scenarios executed end-to-end. Founder-only Level Builder CRUD (create → task-add → publish → archive; separate draft delete), Analytics/Jobs/Flags/Audit tabs, inspect, dry-run, and non-founder guard (level-builder-guard + admin API 403) verified against real production data. Public profile of auditcheckreal shows Newbie level badge + summary-only progress bar (no task rows). Stealth completed the last Explorer task via reaction (real one-time action, per instructions), claim executed, celebration modal (level-celebration + level-celebration-highest 'Highest Available Level Reached') appeared ONLY after backend claim success. FOUND ONE HIGH BUG: after claim of the highest available level, the card does NOT display the 'progress-card-highest' state because the backend /api/progression/me endpoint clobbers ulp.status back to 'active' and claim_available:True on every read (see rca).

critical.issue: After successfully claiming the highest available level, subsequent /me reads return status='active' and summary.claim_available=true even though the persisted user_level_progress row was correctly set to status='highest_level_reached', claim_available=false by claim_level(). services/progression/engine.py::recalc_user recomputes status from scratch from the published level state and overwrites ulp on every persist, losing the highest-level marker. Consequence: the UI never shows progress-card-highest and re-renders the Claim button after a successful claim (repeat clicks are idempotent, so no data corruption, but UX is broken).

ui_bugs.issue: After celebration modal closes, progress-card-highest is not rendered and the Claim button remains visible. Root cause is backend (see backend critical bug) — frontend correctly renders whatever backend returns. If backend fix preserves highest_level_reached status, this UI behavior will self-correct without any FE changes.

ui_bugs.component: AdminLevelBuilder — Archive button on published rows
ui_bugs.issue: The Archive button on published level rows has only title="Archive" and no data-testid="level-archive-{id}". Review spec explicitly requires 'level-archive-*'. Existing testid coverage: level-publish-*, level-pause-*, level-delete-*, level-open-* are all present. Archive was verifiable only by title selector or direct POST /api/admin/progression/levels/{id}/archive. Add data-testid="level-archive-{l.id}" to /app/frontend/src/pages/AdminLevelBuilder.jsx line ~439.

action_items: P1 (backend): Fix services/progression/engine.py::recalc_user() to preserve status='highest_level_reached' and claim_available=false when the user has already successfully claimed the current (level_id, config_version). One approach: at the top of recalc_user, check db.progression_claims for a success record for the current level+version; if found and next_level_after() returns None, force status='highest_level_reached' and claim_available=False in the returned summary and persisted ulp.

P2 (frontend): Add data-testid="level-archive-{l.id}" to the Archive chip button in /app/frontend/src/pages/AdminLevelBuilder.jsx (~line 439) for parity with level-publish-*/level-pause-*/level-delete-*.
P3 (cleanup): One leftover TESTAGENT_iter76_draft level exists in archived state (v1, 0 users). Cannot be hard-deleted because it was published. Leaving archived as intended by the deletion policy.
critical_code_review_comments: engine.py::recalc_user overwrites ulp status regardless of prior claim state — root cause of the highest-level UI regression. See action item P1.
AdminLevelBuilder archive chip lacks data-testid (see FE bug 2). Small oversight — every other action chip has one.

progression.py::my_progression returns 'enabled: False' with NO other fields when display flag is off — client code that expects level/summary/tasks keys may need to null-check. Not a bug per se but a schema shape difference clients must handle.
recalc_user writes summary onto ulp via $set without $currentDate for updated_at (line 178/180); acceptable but future audit correlation might benefit from a monotonic server-side time.

ProgressCard.jsx claim() calls invalidateLevelBadge(username) then await load() — badge cache invalidation is correct, but LevelBadge.useEffect fetches via cache-first (60s TTL) so the badge on other surfaces (feed comments, profile lists) may still show the old level for up to 60s after claim. Consider a broadcast/context to force other LevelBadge instances to refetch.

AdminLevelBuilder mixes anchor-like <button> chips with native browser confirm() dialogs for destructive actions (level-delete). Using window.confirm is fine for now, but a testid-safe modal would be more consistent with the rest of the UI (matters for automated E2E).

rca of the issue:
BUG: highest-level state lost on /me reads.

Reproduction:
1) As stealth (Explorer, 5/5), POST /api/progression/claim {level_id: <explorer_id>} — succeeds, response has highest_level_reached=true and rewards granted.
2) Immediately: db.user_level_progress.find_one({user_id: stealth}) shows status='highest_level_reached', claim_available=False, last_claimed_at set, history count = 2 → CORRECT.
3) Call GET /api/progression/me → response has summary.status='active', summary.claim_available=true, top-level status='active' → WRONG.
4) After that read, db.user_level_progress now shows status='active', claim_available=True (persist=True path overwrote it).

Root cause: services/progression/engine.py::recalc_user (lines 158-180) recomputes 'status' and 'claimable' purely from the current level snapshot state (published/paused/archived) and task completion, and always writes the recomputed summary into ulp via `$set: summary`. It ignores whether the user has already successfully claimed the current (level_id, config_version). When there is no next level (Explorer is the topmost), the correct terminal state 'highest_level_reached' set by claim_level() is silently reverted.

Mitigation (recommended patch — main agent to implement):
  Before returning/persisting summary in recalc_user, add:

    already_claimed = await db.progression_claims.find_one(
        {"user_id": user["id"], "level_id": snap["id"],
         "level_version": snap["config_version"], "status": "success"},
        {"_id": 0, "id": 1})
    if already_claimed:
        nxt = await next_level_after(snap, user)
        if nxt is None:
            status = "highest_level_reached"
            claimable = False
            summary["status"] = status
            summary["claim_available"] = claimable

  (The 'nxt is None' branch means the user is on the terminal level; if a next level exists the engine's separate claim_level → user_level_progress transition already moves them, so this guard only fires for the highest-level scenario.)

  Additionally: recalc_user should ideally never write claim_available=True over a level+version that already has a successful claim on that same version — even if a next level exists, claim.status='success' on this (level, version) is a hard guarantee that the current-level claim was consumed.

Impact scope: pure UX regression on highest-level users. No data corruption because the claim endpoint uses a unique (user_id, level_id, level_version, status='success') index in progression_claims and returns idempotent on duplicate — a repeat click after the state-clobber correctly returns 'idempotent: True' with the original response. Rewards and history are NOT duplicated (verified by test_rewards_never_duplicated + test_claim_idempotent_and_unique in the pre-existing test_progression_core.py suite).
